1.title: Troubleshooting Services and Networking; Monitoring Resource Usage
1.text: Welcome to Module thirteen: Troubleshooting Services and Networking; Monitoring Resource Usage. It covers the exam area Troubleshooting. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, and every task was run on a real cluster, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do three things. Troubleshoot services and networking. Monitor cluster and application resource usage. Practice with six hands-on labs worth forty-two points.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Troubleshooting (thirty percent). Practice in this module: six labs, forty-two points, about forty-two minutes. Exam format: performance-based tasks in a live terminal, scored on the final cluster state. Validated on: Kubernetes version one point thirty-seven point zero.

1.title: Service troubleshooting: walk the path
1.text: Service troubleshooting: walk the path. The figure shows this: The Service path. Exam tip: Walk the path in order: D N S, Service, endpoints, Pod, port.

1.title: Service troubleshooting: walk the path, continued
1.text: Service troubleshooting: walk the path. A request travels: client Pod - greater than D N S name - greater than Service Cluster I P - greater than kube proxy rules - greater than ready Pod I P - greater than container port. Test each hop; the first one that fails is the problem.

1.title: Service troubleshooting: walk the path, continued
1.text: Service troubleshooting: walk the path. one. Name resolves. Test: kube control exec client -- N S lookup web dot net four. If it fails: D N S problem (Core D N S, Pod D N S policy): section three. two. Service exists, right port. Test: kube control get svc web dash o wide; kube control describe svc web. If it fails: wrong namespace or name; port mismatch. three. Service has endpoints. Test: kube control get endpointslices dash l Kubernetes dot io slash service name web. If it fails: empty: selector typo or Pods not Ready. four. Pods Ready. Test: kube control get pods the show labels flag. If it fails: readiness probe failing, crash loop.

1.title: Service troubleshooting: walk the path, continued
1.text: Service troubleshooting: walk the path. five. target Port matches the container. Test: kube control describe svc web, container port. If it fails: "connection refused": wrong target Port. six. Policy blocks it. Test: kube control get netpol dash A. If it fails: timeout (Module nine). seven. Reaches the Pod directly. Test: kube control exec client -- W get -q O- -T three H T T P colon slash slash pod I P. If it fails: works but Service does not: Service config; fails: Pod or policy. Symptom to cause table.

1.title: Service troubleshooting: walk the path, continued
1.text: Service troubleshooting: walk the path. hangs, then times out. no endpoints, Network Policy, or wrong Service name resolving to nothing. "connection refused" immediately. endpoints exist but wrong target Port slash app not listening. "bad address" or "could not resolve". D N S problem. works from one namespace only. short name used across namespaces ( web versus web dot net four ). endpoints list empty, Pods Running. selector mismatch or readiness failing ( zero slash one ) (Labs seven point three, thirteen point three).

1.title: Service troubleshooting: walk the path, continued
1.text: Service troubleshooting: walk the path. Find the right target port without guessing: kube control get pod p dash o json path dot spec dot containers dot ports shows only declared ports; the real listening port is in the image docs or kube control exec p -- net stat -ln (when available). Fix the Service when the task says so; do not change the Deployment.

1.title: Readiness: Running is not Ready
1.text: Readiness: Running is not Ready. A Pod with a failing readiness probe is Running but zero slash one and is removed from the Service endpoints. Look: kube control describe pod - greater than "Readiness probe failed: H T T P probe failed with statuscode: four oh four". Correct the probe path or port in the Deployment (Lab thirteen point three). Do not remove the probe if the task does not say so. Exam tip: A Pod can be Running but not Ready; a failing readiness probe removes it from the endpoints.

1.title: DNS troubleshooting
1.text: D N S troubleshooting. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: DNS troubleshooting, continued
1.text: D N S troubleshooting. no Core D N S Pods. Cause: Deployment scaled to zero (Lab eight point four). Fix: k dash n kube system scale deploy core D N S the replicas flag set to two. Core D N S Crash Loop Back Off, log "Unknown directive". Cause: typo in the Corefile (Lab thirteen point six). Fix: fix the Config Map, k dash n kube system rollout restart deploy core D N S. Pod resolv dot conf shows another nameserver. Cause: Pod dns Policy None or Default (Lab thirteen point five). Fix: recreate the Pod with Cluster First (the default). internal names work, external names fail. Cause: forward target or node D N S problem. Fix: check the Corefile forward line. dns Policy values: Cluster First (default: cluster D N S first), Default (the node's resolver, no cluster names), Cluster First With Host Net (for host Network Pods), None (you supply dns Config ).

1.title: Other network faults to recognize
1.text: Other network faults to recognize. Pods on a node cannot get I P s, node Not Ready. C N I (Container Network Interface) Pod ( kube control get pods dash n kube system dash o wide ) and slash E T C slash cni slash net dot d on the node. Service works from some nodes only. kube proxy Pod on the failing node: k dash n kube system logs kube proxy pod. Node Port unreachable. node I P, node port range, the Service has endpoints, a firewall or security group. Pod-to-Pod traffic blocked. Network Policies in the target namespace (Module nine). Exam tip: Connection refused points to a wrong target Port; a timeout points to no endpoints or a Network Policy.

1.title: Monitoring resource usage
1.text: Monitoring resource usage. kube control top shows current C P U and memory from the Metrics Server. It is a short-window snapshot, not a history. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study. Exam tip: kube control top needs Metrics Server; describe node shows requests and top shows actual use.

1.title: Monitoring resource usage, continued
1.text: Monitoring resource usage. C P U is in millicores ( two hundred fifty millicores equals zero point two five core), memory in Mi. The Metrics Server needs a minute after start before it has data; "metrics not available yet" means wait. kube control top needs the metrics A P I ( kube control get apiservice version one beta one dot metrics dot K eights dot io ) to be Available. If kube control top says "Metrics A P I not available": check the Metrics Server Pod in kube system ( kube control logs deploy slash metrics server dash n kube system ). On clusters with self-signed kubelet certificates it needs the kubelet insecure tls flag (Lab thirteen point two).

1.title: Monitoring resource usage, continued
1.text: Monitoring resource usage. Compare usage with requests and limits: kube control describe node n ends with "Allocated resources" (requests and limits per node), while kube control top node shows actual use. A Pod can be over its request and still be fine; over its memory limit it is O O M-killed (Module eleven). For history and alerts you would use a monitoring system such as Prometheus; the exam objective is kube control top and reading status.

1.title: Lab 13.1: top pods
1.text: Lab thirteen point one: top pods. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace load, three Pods run ( idle a, idle b and busy ). Using the metrics from the Metrics Server, find the Pod that currently uses the most C P U and write only its name to about slash answers slash top pod dot txt on the host. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

1.title: Lab 13.1: top pods, Solution
1.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n load top pods the sort by flag set to cpu. Then kube control dash n load top pods the sort by flag set to cpu the no headers flag head -one awk print one about slash answers slash top pod dot txt. Then cat about slash answers slash top pod dot txt. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

1.title: Lab 13.2: fix metrics server
1.text: Lab thirteen point two: fix metrics server. This task is worth eight points, and you should plan about eight minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. kube control top nodes fails with an error such as "Metrics A P I not available". The Metrics Server runs in kube system but is not ready. Find the cause in its logs and fix it. In this test cluster the kubelets use self-signed serving certificates, so the Metrics Server needs the argument the kubelet insecure tls flag. When done, kube control top nodes must print the usage of all three nodes. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 13.2: fix metrics server, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n kube system get pods dash l K eights app metrics server. Then kube control dash n kube system logs deploy slash metrics server the tail flag set to three. Then kube control dash n kube system patch deployment metrics server the type flag set to json dash p op add, path slash spec slash template slash spec slash containers slash zero slash args or, and so on. Then kube control dash n kube system rollout status deployment metrics server the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then for i in seq one thirty do kube control top nodes slash dev slash null two one break sleep five done. Then kube control top nodes. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 13.3: readiness no endpoints
2.text: Lab thirteen point three: readiness no endpoints. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about seven minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace net three, requests to H T T P colon slash slash shop dot net three fail although the Service shop selects the right Pods. The Pods are Running but not Ready. Find the cause and fix the Deployment shop (do not change the Service) so that H T T P colon slash slash shop dot net three returns the engine X welcome page. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 13.3: readiness no endpoints, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n net three get pods. Then kube control dash n net three describe pod dash l app shop then pipe to grep dash i -A two Readiness probe failed then pipe to head -four. Then kube control dash n net three patch deployment shop the type flag set to json dash p op replace, path slash spec slash template slash spec slash containers slash zero slash readiness Probe slash, and so on. Then kube control dash n net three rollout status deployment shop the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 13.4: wrong targetport
2.text: Lab thirteen point four: wrong targetport. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace net four, the Service web has endpoints, but requests to H T T P colon slash slash web dot net four end with "connection refused". The Pods are Ready and the engine X containers listen on port eighty. Fix the Service (do not touch the Deployment) so that H T T P colon slash slash web dot net four works. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 13.4: wrong targetport, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n net four get endpointslices dash l Kubernetes dot io slash service name web dash o wide. Then kube control dash n net four describe svc web then pipe to grep dash i dash E Port then pipe to Endpoints. Then kube control dash n net four patch svc web the type flag set to json dash p op replace, path slash spec slash ports slash zero slash target Port, value eighty. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 13.5: pod dns policy
2.text: Lab thirteen point five: pod dns policy. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace net five, the Pod lookup cannot resolve any cluster names (for example Kubernetes dot default ). Find the cause in the Pod spec and recreate the Pod lookup (image busy box one dot thirty-six, command sleep three thousand six hundred ) so that it uses the cluster D N S and can resolve Kubernetes dot default dot svc dot cluster dot local. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 13.5: pod dns policy, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n net five get pod lookup dash o json path dot spec dot dns Policy newline. Then kube control dash n net five exec lookup -- cat slash E T C slash resolv dot conf. Then kube control dash n net five delete pod lookup the force flag the grace period flag zero. Then kube control dash n net five run lookup the image flag set to busy box one dot thirty-six the command flag -- sleep three thousand six hundred. Then kube control dash n net five wait the for flag set to condition Ready pod slash lookup the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then kube control dash n net five exec lookup -- N S lookup Kubernetes dot default dot svc dot cluster dot local. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 13.6: coredns bad corefile
2.text: Lab thirteen point six: core D N S bad corefile. This task is worth nine points, and you should plan about nine minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. After a change to the Core D N S configuration, the Core D N S Pods in kube system crash. Name resolution in the cluster is down. Find the error in the Core D N S Pod logs, correct the configuration (the Config Map core D N S ), and restart Core D N S so that two replicas are Ready and Kubernetes dot default dot svc dot cluster dot local resolves. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 13.6: coredns bad corefile, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n kube system get pods dash l K eights app kube dns. Then kube control dash n kube system logs dash l K eights app kube dns the tail flag set to three. Then kube control dash n kube system get configmap core D N S dash o json path dot data dot Corefile sed s slash loadbalanse slash loadbalance or slash tmp slash Corefile dot fixed. Then kube control dash n kube system create configmap core D N S the from file flag set to Corefile slash tmp slash Corefile dot fixed the dry run flag set to client dash o, and so on. Then kube control dash n kube system rollout restart deployment core D N S. Then kube control dash n kube system rollout status deployment core D N S the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Recall Check 1
2.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. A Service times out and get endpointslices is empty. What are the two usual causes? Answer: The selector does not match the Pod labels, or the Pods are not Ready (failing readiness probe). Question two. Endpoints exist but the client gets "connection refused". What is wrong? Answer: The Service target Port does not match the port the container listens on. Question three. What does dns Policy Default do? Answer: The Pod uses the node's D N S resolver, so cluster names do not resolve.

2.title: Recall Check 2
2.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What do you check when N S lookup fails for every cluster name? Answer: The Core D N S Pods (running and ready), their logs, and the Corefile Config Map. Question five. Which command shows the Pod using the most C P U in a namespace? Answer: kube control top pods dash n ns the sort by flag set to cpu. Question six. What component does kube control top depend on? Answer: The Metrics Server (metrics A P I).

2.title: Recall Check 3
2.text: Recall check three. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question seven. How does kube control top node differ from the "Allocated resources" in kube control describe node? Answer: top shows actual current usage; "Allocated resources" shows the sum of requests and limits of scheduled Pods. Question eight. A Pod is Running but zero slash one. Is it receiving Service traffic? Answer: No; it is not Ready and is removed from the endpoints.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Service path: D N S - greater than Service - greater than endpoints - greater than Pod - greater than port. No endpoints: selector typo or readiness failing. Connection refused: wrong target Port. Timeout: no endpoints or Network Policy. D N S: Core D N S Pods or logs or Corefile; Pod dns Policy Cluster First. Monitoring: kube control top nodes, kube control top pods the sort by flag set to cpu, needs Metrics Server. Requests versus use: describe node (allocated) versus top (actual). In the next module, we continue the course.
